gaps.desktop: Inside the lifted card, the loser renders the body text washed out. Notes and checklist items come out about 15 levels lighter than the winner (glyph cores ~#313131/#373737 vs ~#252525/#292929), and the title is greyer too (~#131313 vs ~#080808). So the open to-do reads fainter than the closed rows around it, and the checklist items look like secondary or disabled text next to 'Revise introduction'. The winner keeps the title near-black and the notes and checklist a solid dark grey, so the edited card is the strongest thing on screen. Fix: darken the card's notes and checklist text by one step (~#333 to #2a2a2a) and the title to about #1a1a1a.
gaps.phone: The loser's notes and checklist text are a lighter, thinner grey that is also a hair more tracked. Glyph cores are ~#242424/#2b2b2b against the winner's ~#151515/#1c1c1c, and the notes lines run 2-3px wider. So the three checklist rows (Introduction needs more images, etc.) look faded and less tappable on white. The winner sets notes and checklist in a solid near-black at default tracking, and the task content reads crisply under the black title. Fix: use a darker label colour (~#1c1c1e) for the checklist items and notes and remove the extra letter-spacing.

why: Both pairs are pixel-identical in layout, spacing, icons, separators and shadow. The deciding factor is the tone of the body text inside the open card: the winner keeps notes and checklist items solid and legible, and the loser greys them toward a disabled look.
